clue.text: Acid in the drink? That's most surprising

indicators.note: the sharp word sits inside the drink, so one goes in the other

parts.note: a sling is a cocktail of spirit, sugar and water
acid means sharp-tasting, tart

explanation.surface: Someone finds acid in their cocktail and is shocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something startling causes great surprise or alarm.

clue.text: The code's a mere shop contrivance

indicators.note: a contrivance is something devised, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A secret code turns out to be a shop's ruse.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore is a signalling system using flags held in coded positions.

clue.text: Everyone at home gets exhausted

parts.note: all means everyone
in means at home

explanation.surface: The whole family stays home, worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: All in is informal for tired out.

clue.text: Old-style dress not all will be trying

parts.note: tire is an archaic word for attire, clothing
some is part, not all

explanation.surface: Period costume won't suit everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome means irritating, testing one's patience.

clue.text: Resting, though appearing in act — before Easter

parts.note: do means act, perform
Lent is the forty days of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: An actor idles before the Easter holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'act' suggests the stage; 'Resting' also echoes the actor's word for being out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolent means lazy, idle and inactive.

clue.text: An English convict's up for receiving lead

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A convict is charged with handling stolen lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' suggests handling stolen goods; it hints at galena crystals used in early radio receivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Galena is lead sulphide, the main ore of the metal.

clue.text: Liberal MP taking refreshment outside

indicators.note: the refreshment is placed outside, so the politician's letters go within it

parts.note: ale is a drink, a refreshment
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Liberal member of parliament has a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the party but is the definition, meaning generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal in the sense of generous or plentiful, as a liberal helping.

clue.text: A number were in debt, it's maintained

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number
owed means were in debt

explanation.surface: Several people insist they were in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Avowed means declared or asserted openly.

clue.text: Goody-goody note about worthless concession

indicators.note: the prig and note go round the other word

parts.note: a prig is a smugly virtuous person
vile can mean worthless, base
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A self-righteous memo about a worthless concession.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special right or advantage granted.

clue.text: Poetry written say in a cathedral

indicators.note: the example sits inside the cathedral city

parts.note: Ely in Cambridgeshire has a famous cathedral
say means for example, eg

explanation.surface: Verses composed inside a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, a lament.

clue.text: A woman feeling some sympathy with the Left?

parts.note: mild means to some degree, moderate
red is a person with left-wing sympathies

explanation.surface: A woman who leans slightly to the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: A mild red is someone only somewhat left-wing; joined up, the phrase gives a woman's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildred is a female first name.

clue.text: Beastly row — about time!

indicators.note: the row goes round, so the period of time sits within it

parts.note: a row is a line
an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that a quarrel was overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel but is a line; 'Beastly' means like a beast, here a lion.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means like a lion, so like a beast.

clue.text: Irish money obtained by craft

definitions.meaning: the Irish pound before the euro was the punt
flat-bottomed boats, craft poled along rivers

explanation.surface: Cash obtained in Ireland by cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests cunning, but it means boats.
explanation.definitionFit: The punt was the Irish currency unit, and a punt is also a flat river boat.

clue.text: Personal endurance

parts.note: how long a person endures, read as the length of their life

explanation.definitionFit: Longevity is long life, a person lasting a long time.

clue.text: Trim men ran to work

indicators.note: to work the letters is to knead them into a new order

explanation.surface: Staff jogging to their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges MEN RAN TO; 'Trim' is a noun, decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim is decoration added to clothing or furniture, an embellishment.

clue.text: Foreigner gets roughed up on a new rig

indicators.note: roughing something up messes it about, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An outsider beaten up on a new oil rig.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Norway is foreign to a British solver.

clue.text: A ripping career!

definitions.meaning: a rip or rent in cloth
to career is to rush along headlong

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic cry about a splendid working life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripping' looks like old slang for excellent, and 'career' like a profession; both are other senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a rip in fabric and to dash at speed.

clue.text: A telling trait? Far from it!

definitions.text: A telling trait? Far from it!

parts.words: A telling trait? Far from it!
parts.note: a quality of not telling anything, the opposite of being forthcoming

explanation.definitionFit: Reticence is reluctance to speak or reveal one's thoughts.

clue.text: Continental articles secure support

parts.note: un is a French indefinite article
der is a German definite article
pin means fasten, secure

explanation.surface: European items secure some backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To underpin is to support from below.

clue.text: Start with people caught in advance

indicators.note: people and caught are put inside the word for advance

parts.note: come means approach, advance
men are people
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Begin with a crowd trapped in the forward move.
explanation.definitionFit: Commence is a formal word for begin.

clue.text: In the clear — not by merit

indicators.note: the run sits inside the words that follow, so it is picked from within them

explanation.surface: Getting off scot-free without deserving it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' picks the letters out of 'clear not'; 'In the clear' poses as being acquitted. The definition is loose: to gain something by merit.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve or gain a reward through one's own merit is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Old church leader found not guilty

explanation.surface: A medieval bishop acquitted at trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocent was the name of several popes, and the word also means blameless.

clue.text: Sublime time of year

explanation.surface: A glorious season.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means grand and noble; capitalised, it is a summer month.

clue.text: Most sage is found in Devon and Cornwall.

indicators.note: is is found inside the region, so it is enclosed

parts.note: Devon and Cornwall are English counties in the West Country

explanation.surface: The best herb grows in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' looks like the herb but means wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisest means having the most wisdom.

clue.text: Written about with pride

parts.note: Jane Austen's novel pairs this with Pride in its title

explanation.definitionFit: Pride and Prejudice is Jane Austen's novel, so the word was written about alongside pride.

clue.text: Fold to form petal shape.

indicators.note: to shape the letters is to form them anew

explanation.surface: Folding paper into the shape of a petal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold sewn in cloth.

clue.text: Mock the seamstress with a large figure

parts.note: Mimi is the seamstress heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large figure

explanation.surface: Teasing the dressmaker about her size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large figure' suggests a fat body; it is the numeral 100.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock someone can mean to imitate them, ape them.

clue.text: A New Zealander has to walk backwards above one

indicators.note: in a down clue, above puts one piece before the next
the walking word is read backwards

parts.note: roam means walk about
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Kiwi must walk backwards on top of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the Polynesian people native to New Zealand.

clue.text: The gourmet demands pure ice in a cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are shaken up together

explanation.surface: A fussy diner insists on clean ice in a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person of refined taste in food and drink.

clue.text: Card game — a variety of bridge

definitions.meaning: a gambling game also called twenty-one or blackjack
a floating bridge supported on boats or floats

explanation.surface: A card game described as a form of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' reads as the card game, but is the river crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontoon is the British name for twenty-one, and also a bridge laid on floats.

clue.text: Retrogressive dogma

indicators.note: going backwards gives the same word, so read in reverse it is unchanged

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrogressive' sounds like old-fashioned beliefs, but means the word reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or doctrine held as true.

clue.text: Out of temper, put prong in the fruit

indicators.note: the bad mood is put in the prong, so it goes inside

parts.note: a tine is a prong of a fork
out of temper means angry, and anger is that state

explanation.surface: An irritated person stabs a fork into some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small citrus fruit like a mandarin.
